title: How Can a 500 kg Horse Sleep Standing Up? 🐴
description:
Why can horses sleep standing up? See how the stay apparatus of tendons and ligaments locks a horse's legs, how the kneecap hooks over a bump on the thigh bone like a latch, and why horses still have to lie down for REM dream sleep.

topic: Why can horses sleep standing up?
script: A 500-kilo horse can sleep standing up, and you'd never guess why it doesn't fall. The trick is called the stay apparatus. Tendons and ligaments brace its legs, so the joints lock with almost no muscle effort. In a back leg, the kneecap hooks over a bump on the thigh bone, like a latch clicking shut. The other back leg gets to rest, and every so often it swaps sides. But there's a catch. Dreaming sleep, called REM, relaxes every muscle, and that unlocks the legs. So for REM, a horse has to lie down, about thirty to forty-five minutes a day, often while a buddy stands guard. Miss it for a week or so, and its knees can buckle mid-nap. So, could you sleep standing up, or would you fall flat on your face?
key_facts: The stay apparatus is a system of tendons and ligaments that stabilizes the joints of the forelimbs and hindlimbs so horses can doze standing (SmartPak, TheHorse)

In the hind leg the kneecap (patella) hooks over the medial ridge of the femur to lock the stifle; the horse rests the other hind leg and swaps (standard equine anatomy; TheHorse on the stay apparatus)
REM sleep relaxes all muscle tone, including the stay apparatus, so horses must lie down (sternal or lateral) for it (TheHorse, SmartPak)
Horses need about 30 (SmartPak) to 40-45 (TheHorse) minutes of REM per day; script says 'about thirty to forty-five minutes'
In wild herds one horse often stays awake on watch while others lie down (TheHorse, SmartPak); script hedges with 'often'
REM deprivation lasting more than a week or so can make horses drift into REM standing and collapse, with bowing knees (Houpt and Greening via TheHorse)
Average horse weight ~500 kg (common figure for a riding horse)
